minutes.headline: Select Board voted to file as intervener in the FERC pipeline case and join a municipal gas pipeline coalition.
minutes.summary: The board approved a Salvation Army boot drive, signed school building project budget revision requests, and voted to intervene in the pipeline filing and join the Northeast municipal gas pipeline coalition. Committee reports covered the cable survey in tax bills, stormwater, conservation, a solar variance, and the start of FY17 budget planning.

what_happened.line: The Select Board took up joining the FERC pipeline case as an intervener and joining a Northeast municipal gas pipeline coalition; the minutes list the vote outcome as not audible.
The board approved the Salvation Army boot drive for December twelfth at the center of town and CVS intersection, as presented.
The board took up authorizing the chair to sign school building budget revision requests for change orders; the minutes list the vote outcome as not audible.
The revision requests moved money from construction contingency to change orders, and one clerical correction moved an MSBA-flagged item to advertising.
The town manager will try to fit both the cable survey blurb and a school project update into the tax bill mailing.

why_it_matters: Intervening in the pipeline case puts the town on the record in a federal proceeding, and the main cost is ongoing town counsel review, which is paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
Change orders drawn from the school building project's construction contingency leave less reserve for later surprises, so the project's final cost depends on what remains.
The tax bill mailing is where residents will see the cable survey and the school project update.
